explanation: For each distinct dictionary word, backtrack from every board cell through adjacent matching characters. Mark cells on the current path and unmark on return so a path cannot reuse a cell.
timeComplexity: O(W times R times C times 4^L) upper bound for W words, R rows, C columns, and maximum word length L.
spaceComplexity: O(R times C + L + W) auxiliary space excluding returned words.
attribution: Original EPI Practice C# implementation, reusing and refining the repository-authored Blind75 algorithm fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: For a fixed word, the search path spells exactly its matched prefix and the visited marks contain precisely that path’s cells. Extending to an unvisited orthogonal matching cell preserves the invariant, and unmarking on return restores it for other branches. Trying every start finds every realizable distinct dictionary word and rejects paths requiring diagonals or cell reuse.
walkthrough: On board ["ab","cd"], "ab" and "ac" follow the top row and left column; "bd" follows the right column; "cab" follows c→a→b. "ad" would require a diagonal and is rejected. Return ["ab","ac","bd","cab"] in any order.
edgeCases: Words may share board cells across different searches.
One word’s path cannot reuse a cell.
Repeated dictionary entries produce one returned word.
Only horizontal and vertical moves are allowed.
